title: An insulated gate controls the channel
caption: The gate acts through an electric field. It is separated from the conducting channel by an insulator rather than inserted into the source–drain current path.

nodes.label: Gate
nodes.detail: Changes channel conduction through the dielectric.

nodes.label: Channel
nodes.detail: Its conduction depends on the gate condition.

nodes.label: Drain
nodes.detail: Collects carriers passing through the channel.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: A fin gives the gate more access to the channel
caption: The planar view cuts along the source–drain path. The FinFET view cuts across its fin, where the gate covers the top and both sidewalls. These are different section directions, chosen to show the controlling surfaces.

nodes.label: Planar
nodes.detail: The main gate lies above the channel region.

nodes.label: FinFET
nodes.detail: The gate wraps across the top and sides of a fin.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Gate-all-around changes the channel geometry
caption: Released sheets allow the gate to surround the channel. Access, isolation and contacts must still fit around the switching structure.

nodes.label: Fin channel
nodes.detail: A vertical fin exposes multiple sides to the gate.

nodes.label: Gated nanosheets
nodes.detail: After sheet release, dielectric and gate material surround each horizontal channel.

nodes.label: Circuit contacts
nodes.detail: Terminals still need connections to useful wiring.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Connections climb through insulating levels
caption: Vias join wiring levels, while the surrounding insulator keeps separate routes apart. Upper levels often support longer routes and power distribution.

nodes.label: Local wiring
nodes.detail: Short connections close to the transistors.

nodes.label: Device contacts
nodes.detail: Connect transistor terminals to the wiring system.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Smaller wires can cost more signal delay
caption: A narrower conducting cross-section raises resistance; surfaces and grain boundaries can add another penalty. Nearby conductors also create capacitance.

nodes.label: Wide conductor
nodes.detail: More cross-section is available for current.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.

title: Separate the power route from signal wiring
caption: Backside power delivery moves selected power connections to the opposite face. The implementation must still control resistance, alignment and thermal behavior.

nodes.label: Frontside routing
nodes.detail: Signals and power compete for wiring resources above devices.

nodes.label: Backside power
nodes.detail: Power arrives through dedicated connections below the device layer.

note: Conceptual schematic; geometry is not to scale.
